- When sentiment turns strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 3–10 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overestimates in early 30-day horizon; apply 3–7% downward bias for first 10–15 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.67 → 1.00 → 0.00), model fails to adjust; apply mean-reversion correction to mid-range of forecast.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price history shows no clear trend, model often overfits recent noise; use 3–5% smoothing filter on forecast.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after model peak, apply “lag correction”: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 7–14 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.
